column1: # MUST_CONTAIN.tsv -- the BOM for v1.0.69.
# THIS FILE IS THE SOURCE. CM051 VENDORS IT.
# CM051 scripts/sync_cut_bom.sh copies this file into cuts/v1.0.69/ there and
# records the OS003 commit it came from in cuts/BOM_PIN.
# EVERY ROW SAYS ONE OF THREE THINGS AND NEVER A FOURTH
#   gate:<workflow>#<what>  a CI gate that FAILS on the real pre-fix tree
#   artefact:<sha8>#<what>  measured on the published artefact itself
#   needs-walk:<ver>#<what> UNPROVEN, and here is exactly what to look at
# WHY THIS CUT EXISTS, IN ONE LINE
# v1.0.68 INSTALLED CLEAN -- 39 steps, 38 of 38 reached, one terminal
# DONE status=ok, 0 errors, 0 aborts, walk verdict PASS. Two install.sh fixes
# merged after its pin and are unwalked. This cut carries them, and Andy is
# walking the result BY HAND ON A FRESH ACCOUNT (archie2 on the Mini 16),
# which is the first walk of any kind to launch the .app rather than run the
# install.sh inside it.
# BOTH ROWS WERE EXECUTED AGAINST THE PRE-FIX TREE
# A wiring table proves a test RUNS, not that it can FAIL. So both were run
# against install.sh at f60307ad, the v1.0.68 pin, with the fixed tree as the
# control:
#   #1520 diagnostics persist        rc=2  CANNOT-RUN pre-fix
#   #1515 killed converge recorded   rc=1  FAILS      pre-fix
#   CONTROL: both return rc=0 on the fixed tree, so a pre-fix non-zero is the
#            change and not a broken harness.
# The CANNOT-RUN is weaker evidence than the FAIL and is recorded as weaker:
# it refuses because the persister it extracts BY NAME did not exist before the
# fix. A gate that refuses is a gate that would block a regression, and rc=2 is
# a refusal, never a pass.
# LANDED, AND HOW THAT WAS ESTABLISHED
# Both refs are ANCESTORS of 7cd88739, the CM051 pin, checked with
# `git merge-base --is-ancestor`, not asserted. Ancestry is valid in ONE
# direction only: TRUE proves landed.

THE DIAGNOSTICS MUST SURVIVE THE RUN THAT PRODUCED THEM. OSTLER_DIAG_DIR is a mktemp directory under TMPDIR, which on macOS is /var/folders/<per-user>/T and is purged on the OS schedule, not ours. install.sh names it in 82 places including three of the loudest warnings we ship -- the half-migrated-store warning, the calendar extractor failure and the conversation-ingest structural break. Each told a customer to read a file at a transient path. The migration warning exists to make someone STOP AND LOOK and it named a file they could not find the next day. Now copied to ~/.ostler/diagnostics/<utc> at 0700, best-effort by construction: an install must never fail because a log copy did not.

A KILLED CONVERGE IS RECORDED, AND NO LONGER CALLS ITSELF HARMLESS. install.sh kills the identity resolver on a 300s budget: SIGTERM, 2s, SIGKILL. The comment beside it claimed nothing is lost because the resolver commits each merge as it goes. That is true per MERGE and false per SPARQL UPDATE -- merge_persons is eight updates, identifiers move at step 1 and the authorising tombstone is written at step 6, and SIGKILL cannot be trapped. The kill path now writes ~/.ostler/state/dedupe-converge.killed with the time, the budget and the risk, because the ABSENCE of the .done marker cannot distinguish killed-at-budget from exited-non-zero.
